ConocoPhillips rose 1.3% today as oil markets tightened on multiple fronts. Diesel prices are expected to stay elevated through 2027 due to refinery capacity constraints, which boosts margins for integrated oil and gas companies like this one. Additionally, Middle East tensions—including fresh fighting over Red Sea control and ongoing U.S.-Iran friction—continue to create supply-side anxiety, with global oil inventories still depleted and taking years to rebuild according to Saudi Aramco's leadership.

The company also stands to benefit from momentum around U.S. energy infrastructure projects; recent headlines show the administration actively promoting Alaska LNG deals to allies, which fits a broader push to expand domestic energy exports. With Brent crude near $100 a barrel and refinery economics favorable, the stock has climbed steadily over the past week as geopolitical and supply risks keep energy markets supported.
